summary.text: Define \(x_0=1, x_1=-2\) and \(x_{n+2}=-4x_{n+1}-64x_n\); both \(x_{n+1}^2\) and the odd-indexed terms satisfy the recurrence \(u_{n+3}=-48u_{n+2}+3072u_{n+1}+262144u_n\). Their first three values agree, so induction gives \(a(2n+1)=x_{n+1}^2\) for every \(n\).

full_proof.text:
Let \((a_n)_{n\ge 0}\) be the integer sequence defined by
\[
a_0=-1,\qquad a_1=4,\qquad a_2=176,\qquad a_3=3136,
\]
and, for every \(n\ge 0\),
\[
a_{n+4}=-4a_{n+3}+256a_{n+1}+4096a_n.
\]
We shall prove that for every nonnegative integer \(n\), the odd-indexed term \(a_{2n+1}\) is a square of an integer.

Define an auxiliary integer sequence \((x_n)_{n\ge 0}\) by
\[
x_0=1,\qquad x_1=-2,
\]
and
\[
x_{n+2}=-4x_{n+1}-64x_n\qquad(n\ge 0).
\]
We will prove the more precise identity
\[
\boxed{a_{2n+1}=x_{n+1}^2}
\]
for every \(n\ge 0\).

First we derive a recurrence for the squares of the \(x_n\). Fix \(n\ge 0\), and put
\[
u=x_{n+1},\qquad v=x_{n+2}.
\]
Applying the defining recurrence once gives
\[
x_{n+3}=-4v-64u.
\]
Applying it again gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
x_{n+4}
  &=-4x_{n+3}-64x_{n+2}\\
  &=-4(-4v-64u)-64v\\
  &=256u-48v.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
&-48x_{n+3}^2+3072x_{n+2}^2+262144x_{n+1}^2\\
&\quad=-48(-4v-64u)^2+3072v^2+262144u^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Expanding the square,
\[
(-4v-64u)^2=16v^2+512uv+4096u^2,
\]
so the right-hand side becomes
\[
\begin{aligned}
&-48(16v^2+512uv+4096u^2)+3072v^2+262144u^2\\
&=(-768+3072)v^2-24576uv+(-196608+262144)u^2\\
&=2304v^2-24576uv+65536u^2\\
&=(256u-48v)^2\\
&=x_{n+4}^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus, for every \(n\ge 0\),
\[
\boxed{x_{n+4}^2=-48x_{n+3}^2+3072x_{n+2}^2+262144x_{n+1}^2.}\tag{1}
\]

We next derive a corresponding six-step recurrence for \(a_n\). Fix \(n\ge 0\). The original recurrence at indices \(n+5\) and \(n+6\) says
\[
a_{n+5}=-4a_{n+4}+256a_{n+2}+4096a_{n+1}
\]
and
\[
a_{n+6}=-4a_{n+5}+256a_{n+3}+4096a_{n+2}.
\]
Substituting the first equation into the second yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{n+6}
&=-4\bigl(-4a_{n+4}+256a_{n+2}+4096a_{n+1}\bigr)
  +256a_{n+3}+4096a_{n+2}\\
&=16a_{n+4}+3072a_{n+2}+256a_{n+3}-16384a_{n+1}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Meanwhile, the recurrence at index \(n+4\) is
\[
a_{n+4}=-4a_{n+3}+256a_{n+1}+4096a_n.
\]
Multiplying this equality by \(-64\) and rearranging gives
\[
256a_{n+3}-16384a_{n+1}=-64a_{n+4}+262144a_n.
\]
Substituting this into the preceding expression for \(a_{n+6}\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{n+6}
&=16a_{n+4}+3072a_{n+2}-64a_{n+4}+262144a_n\\
&=-48a_{n+4}+3072a_{n+2}+262144a_n.
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{a_{n+6}=-48a_{n+4}+3072a_{n+2}+262144a_n}\tag{2}
\]
for every \(n\ge 0\).

Now consider only the odd-indexed terms. Define
\[
b_n=a_{2n+1}\qquad(n\ge 0).
\]
In (2), replace \(n\) by \(2m+1\). This gives
\[
a_{2m+7}=-48a_{2m+5}+3072a_{2m+3}+262144a_{2m+1}.
\]
In terms of \(b_m\), this is
\[
\boxed{b_{m+3}=-48b_{m+2}+3072b_{m+1}+262144b_m}\tag{3}
\]
for every \(m\ge 0\).

On the other hand, define
\[
c_n=x_{n+1}^2.
\]
Equation (1) says exactly that
\[
\boxed{c_{m+3}=-48c_{m+2}+3072c_{m+1}+262144c_m}\tag{4}
\]
for every \(m\ge 0\). Thus \((b_n)\) and \((c_n)\) satisfy the same third-order recurrence. It remains to compare their first three terms.

For \(n=0\),
\[
b_0=a_1=4,
\]
while
\[
c_0=x_1^2=(-2)^2=4.
\]
Therefore \(b_0=c_0\).

For \(n=1\), the auxiliary recurrence gives
\[
x_2=-4x_1-64x_0=-4(-2)-64(1)=8-64=-56.
\]
Hence
\[
c_1=x_2^2=(-56)^2=3136=a_3=b_1.
\]

For \(n=2\), first compute
\[
x_3=-4x_2-64x_1=-4(-56)-64(-2)=224+128=352,
\]
so
\[
c_2=x_3^2=352^2=123904.
\]
To compute \(b_2=a_5\), we first use the recurrence for \(a_4\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_4
&=-4a_3+256a_1+4096a_0\\
&=-4(3136)+256(4)+4096(-1)\\
&=-12544+1024-4096\\
&=-15616.
\end{aligned}
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_5
&=-4a_4+256a_2+4096a_1\\
&=-4(-15616)+256(176)+4096(4)\\
&=62464+45056+16384\\
&=123904.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(b_2=a_5=123904=c_2\).

We now prove \(b_n=c_n\) for all \(n\ge 0\) by induction governed by the three-term window in recurrences (3) and (4). The equality has just been established for \(n=0,1,2\). Suppose that for some \(m\ge 0\),
\[
b_m=c_m,\qquad b_{m+1}=c_{m+1},\qquad b_{m+2}=c_{m+2}.
\]
Using (3), then these three equalities, and finally (4), we get
\[
\begin{aligned}
b_{m+3}
&=-48b_{m+2}+3072b_{m+1}+262144b_m\\
&=-48c_{m+2}+3072c_{m+1}+262144c_m\\
&=c_{m+3}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the equality propagates from each three consecutive indices to the next one. Induction proves that \(b_n=c_n\) for every nonnegative integer \(n\).

Recalling the definitions of \(b_n\) and \(c_n\), we have proved
\[
a_{2n+1}=x_{n+1}^2
\]
for every \(n\ge 0\). Since each \(x_{n+1}\) is an integer, this explicitly expresses every odd-indexed term \(a_{2n+1}\) as a perfect square. Hence, for every nonnegative integer \(n\), \(a(2n+1)\) is a perfect square.
